lines: How did the Dutch build land from the sea?
This is Flevopolder: 970 square kilometers. Bigger than Singapore.
First they cut the sea off with a dam. Then they built a ring of dikes in the shallow water.
And pumped it dry. The south fell dry in 1968.
On the old seabed, they built a city from nothing. Almere.
Its first homes went up in 1976. Today over 200,000 people live there.
Fifty-eight years ago, fish swam here. That's how the Dutch built land from the sea.
